title: The Lion, the Bear, and the Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion and a Bear were fighting for possession of a kid, which they had both seized at the same moment.
sentences.zh: 一头狮子和一头熊为争夺一只小山羊而厮打，它们同时抓住了它。

sentences.en: The battle was long and fierce, and at length both of them were exhausted …
sentences.zh: 这场恶斗又久又猛烈，到最后两个都力气耗尽……

sentences.en: … and lay upon the ground severely wounded and gasping for breath.
sentences.zh: ……倒在地上，伤得很重，喘息不止。

sentences.en: A Fox had all the time been prowling round and watching the fight …
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸一直在周围徘徊，看着这场打斗……

sentences.en: … and when he saw the combatants lying there too weak to move, he slipped in and seized the kid, and ran off with it.
sentences.zh: ……见两个斗士躺在那儿连动的力气都没有，便溜进去抓起小羊跑掉了。

sentences.en: They looked on helplessly, and one said to the other, "Here we've been mauling each other all this while …
sentences.zh: 它们无可奈何地看着，其中一个对另一个说：「我们厮打了这么久……」

sentences.en: … and no one the better for it except the Fox!"
sentences.zh: 「……结果除了狐狸，谁也没捞着好处！」

title: The Two Soldiers and the Robber
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Two Soldiers travelling together were set upon by a Robber.
sentences.zh: 两个同行的士兵遭到一个强盗袭击。

sentences.en: One of them ran away, but the other stood his ground …
sentences.zh: 其中一个跑了，另一个却站住不退……

sentences.en: … and laid about him so lustily with his sword that the Robber was fain to fly and leave him in peace.
sentences.zh: ……挥剑奋勇砍杀，强盗只好逃走，不再惹他。

sentences.en: When the coast was clear the timid one ran back, and, flourishing his weapon, cried in a threatening voice, "Where is he?
sentences.zh: 危险过去后，那个胆小的跑回来，挥舞着兵器，用威胁的口吻叫道：「他在哪儿？

sentences.en: Let me get at him, and I'll soon let him know whom he's got to deal with."
sentences.zh: 让我去会他，我很快就让他知道惹的是谁。」

sentences.en: But the other replied, "You are a little late, my friend …
sentences.zh: 可另一个答道：「朋友，你来得晚了点……」

sentences.en: … I only wish you had backed me up just now, even if you had done no more than speak …
sentences.zh: 「……我只盼你刚才能给我撑腰，哪怕只是说句话也好……」

sentences.en: … for I should have been encouraged, believing your words to be true.
sentences.zh: 「……那样我也会受些鼓舞，以为你的话是真的。

sentences.en: As it is, calm yourself, and put up your sword: there is no further use for it.
sentences.zh: 事已如此，你安静些，把剑收起来吧，它已经没用了。

sentences.en: You may delude others into thinking you're as brave as a lion: but I know that, at the first sign of danger, you run away like a hare."
sentences.zh: 你或许能骗别人相信你勇猛如狮；可我知道，一有危险，你跑得比兔子还快。」

title: The Wolf, the Mother, and Her Child
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A hungry Wolf was prowling about in search of food.
sentences.zh: 一只饥饿的狼四处游荡觅食。

sentences.en: By and by, attracted by the cries of a Child, he came to a cottage.
sentences.zh: 不久，他被一个孩子的哭声引来，来到一间小屋前。

sentences.en: As he crouched beneath the window, he heard the Mother say to the Child, "Stop crying, do! or I'll throw you to the Wolf."
sentences.zh: 他蹲在窗下，听见母亲对孩子说：「别哭了！再哭就把你扔给狼。」

sentences.en: Thinking she really meant what she said, he waited there a long time in the expectation of satisfying his hunger.
sentences.zh: 他以为她当真如此，便在那儿等了很久，指望能填饱肚子。

sentences.en: In the evening he heard the Mother fondling her Child and saying, "If the naughty Wolf comes, he shan't get my little one …
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，他听见母亲爱抚着孩子说：「要是那坏狼敢来，他休想碰我的小宝贝……」

sentences.en: … Daddy will kill him."
sentences.zh: 「……爸爸会打死他。」

sentences.en: The Wolf got up in much disgust and walked away …
sentences.zh: 狼十分厌恶地起身走开……

sentences.en: … "As for the people in that house," said he to himself, "you can't believe a word they say."
sentences.zh: ……「那一家人，」他自言自语，「说的话一个字都不能信。」

sentences.en: A Cat pounced on a Cock, and cast about for some good excuse for making a meal off him, for Cats don't as a rule eat Cocks …
sentences.zh: 一只猫扑住一只公鸡，琢磨着找个好借口把他吃掉，因为猫通常并不吃公鸡……

sentences.en: … and she knew she ought not to.
sentences.zh: ……她也知道自己不该如此。

sentences.en: At last she said, "You make a great nuisance of yourself at night by crowing and keeping people awake …
sentences.zh: 最后她说：「你夜里打鸣，吵得人睡不着，实在讨厌……」

sentences.en: … so I am going to make an end of you."
sentences.zh: 「……所以我要结果了你。」

sentences.en: But the Cock defended himself by saying that he crowed in order that men might wake up and set about the day's work in good time …
sentences.zh: 公鸡为自己辩解说，他打鸣是为了让人们醒来、按时开始一天的活儿……

sentences.en: … and that they really couldn't very well do without him.
sentences.zh: ……人们实在少不得他。

sentences.en: "That may be," said the Cat, "but whether they can or not, I'm not going without my dinner"; and she killed and ate him.
sentences.zh: 「也许吧，」猫说，「可不管他们少不少得，我总不能不吃晚饭。」说完就把他弄死吃了。

sentences.en: The want of a good excuse never kept a villain from crime.
sentences.zh: 恶人从不会因为找不到好借口就不作恶。
